# The site version, the app and the play session

## THE APP (moved from the hard rules)

- **THE APP (installable, offline; `manifest.webmanifest`, `sw.js`, `shared/app.js`, `offline.html`, icons in `shared/app/` from `tools/app-icon.html`).** `checkVersion` writes every page's app tags (manifest link, apple-touch-icon, apple-mobile-web-app-* with a black-translucent status bar) and loads `shared/app.js` (`A.ROOT` = the site root from version.js's own address), so a new page needs only the three version lines + its own `theme-color`; `<meta name="arcade-app" content="off">` above them = no app.js (the avatar card, shown inside other sites). `A.v(url)` uses `A.pageVersion` (the page's own checkVersion value), so a kept old page never loads new files. THE SERVICE WORKER (`sw.js`, root, registered by app.js ONLY when VERSION isn't 'dev'; a leftover one is unregistered in dev): one cache per version `band-arcade-<version>`; the deploy (stamp-version.py) writes VERSION + `FILES` (every served file: a content fingerprint + 'p' stored at install: html/js/css/woff2/manifest/icons, or 'u' on first use: sounds, pictures); an install COPIES unchanged files from the older cache, downloads the rest; activate deletes older caches + `clients.claim()`. Pages (navigations) and version.js: network first with `cache: 'no-cache'`, the stored copy only when the network fails, else `offline.html` ("You're offline. Games you've played before still work!"). Everything else: cache first; `?v=<another version>` = network only, never stored (no mixed versions); requests with cache reload/no-cache/no-store or a Range header, other sites (THE LEADERBOARD) and non-GET are never touched. UPDATES (app.js): checked on load, when the page comes back on screen and every 30 min; a waiting worker whose version = this page's is activated silently; an older open page gets the banner `.app-update` "New version ready — tap to update" (hidden `html.in-play`; the tap = skip-waiting + reload); ignored = applied at the next open. INSTALL: `A.App.installButton(el)` (the floor's sound panel) only with `Arcade.TEACHER.SHOW_INSTALL_PROMPT` (teacher-settings.js, false until the final address), `beforeinstallprompt` is always held for it; iPad = the steps with pictures. BRING YOUR PROGRESS: the app's first launch (standalone + nothing in localStorage when app.js runs: `bandarcade.app-welcome` 'ask' → 'done', outside the Backup Code) on the floor, after PRESS START and before pick mode (`A.App.welcome(then)` in arcade.js): paste a Backup Code or Start fresh. `A.App.micHelp()` adds "open Band Arcade in Safari instead" to mic-gate's errors in the app. SAFE AREAS: `.wrap`, `.overlay` and every full-screen layout pad with `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. `?standalone` pretends to be the app (tests); `A.App.state()`. Tests: tests/app.spec.js (stamps two copies with `testv1`/`testv2`).
- SOUNDS AND THE OFFLINE COPY: sounds are 'u' files (stored the first time they're used), fingerprinted like everything else, so when a sound file shrinks (`tools/compress-sounds.py`, [sound.md](sound.md)) the next version stamp makes each device download the smaller file once, the next time it plays it; nothing in sw.js lists sounds by hand. A push that changes a sound is deployed by `compress-sounds.yml` after compressing (pages.yml's `sounds` job skips its own deploy for it), so a version never publishes the big upload.

## THE DEPLOY PIPELINE (stamp → minify → fingerprint → publish)

- **The repository is never minified; never commit minified files.** Mat edits and double-click tests the plain files. Only the copy GitHub Pages publishes is changed, on every push to main, by `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (on its own checkout; nothing is committed back):
  1. `tools/stamp-version.py --stamp-only <id>`: the version into `shared/version.js` and every page (`?v=<id>` on every local .js/.css tag, `checkVersion('<id>')`).
  2. `tools/minify-site.py`: every served .js and .css minified IN PLACE with esbuild (pinned: `ESBUILD_VERSION` there, the same as `tests/package.json`), one file at a time in transform mode: `--minify --target=safari15,chrome100 --legal-comments=none` (CSS: `--loader=css`). Same names, folders, script tags and load order. NEVER `--bundle` and never a `--format`, so top-level names (the classic scripts share globals) and `document.currentScript` (sfx.js, portraits.js, marquees.js, backgrounds.js, avatar-badge.js) keep working. Not touched: `sw.js`, `shared/vendor/`, `*.min.js`, the HTML pages and their inline scripts, JSON and every other file, the unserved folders (tests, tools, .github), and any file whose FIRST LINE is `/* keep-unminified */` (featured.js, leaderboard-config.js, teacher-settings.js: Mat may fix them live in GitHub's editor, and the deployed copy reads the same). If esbuild fails on a file, that file is published as it is with a warning; if esbuild can't be installed, nothing is minified (a warning). Never a broken deploy. The log lists each file before → after, the totals and the lobby's total (about 45 % less JavaScript).
  3. `tools/stamp-version.py --fingerprints-only <id>`: sw.js's `VERSION` and `FILES`, fingerprinting the files AS PUBLISHED (minified), so an update re-downloads only files whose minified bytes changed. (`stamp-version.py <id>` with no flag still does 1 + 3 in one go.)
  4. `tests/` is removed, the folder is published.
- **Tested before it merges:** `tests.yml` runs the whole suite twice in both browsers: on the repository's files and on a PUBLISHED copy (`tests/deploy.js`: the same three steps, version `testbuild`, served with `ARCADE_SITE`). The app tests (`app.spec.js`) always deploy their two versions this way. See [testing.md](testing.md).
- **Reading an error from a student's device:** each minified .js has a source map next to it (`<file>.js.map`, holding the original source; its last line `//# sourceMappingURL=<file>.js.map`). With DevTools open, errors and breakpoints show the real file and line (the original appears as `original-source:///shared/<file>.js`). The maps are only fetched by DevTools: they are left out of the app's offline copy (`.map` in stamp-version.py's NOT_SERVED). Without DevTools, the line in an error message is the minified one: open the same address with DevTools to map it.
- **DON'T BUNDLE (and don't "optimize" this later).** Combining scripts into one file would break `document.currentScript` (the files above find their folders with it), stop one failing script from being isolated from the rest, and make every game page re-download shared code it already has cached. GitHub Pages serves HTTP/2 (40 small files cost little), and the installed app serves them from its offline copy anyway. Hard rule: never add a bundler or a build step to the repository; deploy-time minify only.

## ON-DEMAND SCRIPTS (the floor's rarely used features)

- `Arcade.need(paths, {quiet})` (shared/version.js, every page): a Promise; adds each script (an address from the site root, e.g. `'shared/prizes.js'`) ONCE, in order, as a plain `<script>` tag with `Arcade.v`'s `?v=`, so it works from a double-clicked file (no fetch, no eval). A second call returns the same Promise; a script the page already lists is never added again. While it loads, the button tapped in the last 1.5 s gets the UI kit's spinner (`.ui-spin`, `aria-busy`, after 150 ms so a stored file shows none); a failure (offline and never stored) shows the toast "Couldn't open that. Check your connection and try again." and the next call tries again. `{quiet: true}`: no spinner or toast (the caller has its own fallback).
- `Arcade.lazy(name, paths, methods, extra)`: a STAND-IN `Arcade[name]` (`{lazy: true, load()}` + each method: loads the scripts, then calls the real one, a Promise of its answer, `undefined` if it couldn't load). The real script replaces it. Never replaces a real one the page already has.
- **The lobby's on-demand scripts** (index.html doesn't list them; arcade.js "THE ON-DEMAND SCRIPTS" makes the stand-ins): `shared/prizes.js` (+ `shared/locker.js`, its pictures) the PRIZE COUNTER (lobby sign, the aisle's counter in 2D and 3D, the avatar badge's menu, the event panel's shelf line, `?prizes`); `shared/backup.js` (Settings → Backup / Restore, the player card's button, the app's first-launch "Bring your progress", which starts loading it when the panel shows); `leaderboard-screen.js` (the LEADERBOARD button; arcade.js now shows and wires `#lbBtn`); `shared/avatar-creator.js` and `shared/locker.js` (the avatar badge's `AvatarBadge.edit` / `Locker.open`, which already loaded them on game pages; "Create your player?" is `AvatarBadge.offer` in avatar-badge.js so it shows at once); `arcade3d.js` with three.js (`load3D` in arcade.js, the first time a zone opens in 3D; the 2D view never loads them, a failed load falls back to 2D). Kept at load because the lobby uses them at once: `shared/tokens.js` (the sign's balance and wish), `shared/avatar-badge.js` (the Locker's counts and NEW dot). Their stylesheets stay in index.html's `<head>`.
- **They stay 'p' in sw.js** (stored at install, like every .js), so the installed app opens them offline on the first tap.
- **A new rarely used lobby feature should load the same way** (a stand-in in arcade.js, or `Arcade.need` before its first use). `tests/perf.spec.js` keeps the published lobby's JavaScript under a budget and fails, naming the biggest files, when a change pushes it over. Game pages still list their own scripts (not changed yet: Music Highway loads 44 scripts, ≈ 1290 KB unminified, ≈ 690 KB published).

## THE PLAY SESSION

- THE PLAY SESSION (`Arcade.session`, shared/version.js: `has(k)`, `mark(k)`, `reset()`): once-per-session flags (the mic reminder `'mic-reminder'`, Music Highway's `'mh-calibrated-speaker'` / `'-headphones'`). A session = from opening the arcade until the tab is closed or a page is RELOADED: the flags live in memory and are handed to the next page of the same tab through `window.name` (never localStorage/sessionStorage); a reload (navigation type 'reload') starts a new one. Tests: tests/play-session.spec.js.
